summary: CONVENTIONS §5 refined by the first compound component. Two rules that were unambiguous for Button (a single element) diverged for Input. (1) ref: form controls forward to the interactive element rather than the outermost node — a ref to a wrapper cannot focus the field, read a value, or be handed to a form library, which is every reason a caller takes one. (2) className: always lands on the OUTERMOST node so sizing behaves predictably, while native props go to the element that owns them; Input initially put className on the control while spreading rest onto the input, which was inconsistent in a way no gate could see. Both now have browser regression tests asserting computed width and attribute placement.

migration.manual: Components authored before this: check that className reaches the outermost node and that a form control's ref reaches its interactive element.
